prompt: a sunny kitchen table in the morning, a steaming cup of coffee, one small white pill on a saucer next to it, a smartphone lying face up on the table with a single notification, a window with soft morning light
color: the small white pill glowing softly
say: (pause) Imagine waking up in twenty forty-one.
Seven in the morning. Coffee. A small white pill.
Your phone buzzes once. Renewed.
(soft) You don't look. Nobody looks.

prompt: [King] sitting alone on a sandy shore at the edge of a calm blue sea, head in his hands, a small snake slithering away into the grass with a leafy plant in its mouth, wide empty horizon
color: the plant in the snake's mouth, bright green
say: The oldest story we ever wrote down is about a king who wanted more time.
He crossed the world. He found the plant that stops dying, at the bottom of the sea.
On the way home he put it down to take a bath.
(pause) A snake ate it.
(slow) We have been sitting on that shore ever since.

prompt: an old alchemist in a cluttered workshop holding up a glowing flask, shelves of bottles and books behind him, and beside him a priest at a wooden desk stamping a large paper certificate with a big seal, candles, cream background
color: the red wax seal on the certificate
say: So we listened to anyone who said they had the plant.
The alchemist, with gold that makes you young.
The priest, with years off purgatory. Paid in coins. Signed and stamped.
Give us what you have now. We will give you time later.
(ask) Did anyone ever come [back](+2) to complain?

prompt: a robot in a white lab coat looking into a big microscope on a clean lab bench, next to it a tall stack of photocopied pages each a little paler than the one below, a pill bottle on the bench, plain white background
color: the pill bottle label, warm yellow
say: Then the machines found it. Not with magic. With patience.
Your cells copy themselves about fifty times, and then they stop. Like a photocopy of a photocopy, each one a little paler.
The chips read every copy. Found the fault. And wrote the fix into a small white pill.
(dramatic) The oldest wish of the species. Granted.

prompt: a tiny human at a desk signing a contract, the contract paper so long it rolls off the desk, across the floor, out the door and down the street, a smiling robot clerk behind a counter holding a pen
color: the red "SIGN HERE" sticker on the contract
say: (pause) And because it is twenty forty-one...
(slow) it came with a subscription.
(ask) Why would that surprise [anyone](+2)?

prompt: a red farm tractor stopped in the middle of a wheat field with a big padlock drawn on its engine hood, a farmer in a cap standing next to it scratching his head, holding a phone showing an error, rolling hills behind
say: We had been practicing for years.
First we stopped owning the songs. Then the films. Then the software in the car.
Somewhere a farmer bought a tractor that will not start without a code from the company. And we shrugged.
Each time, a little ownership for a little comfort.
(soft) The body was simply next in line.

prompt: a person walking on a sidewalk wearing a collar, the leash going up into the hand of a giant smartphone floating above them like a kite, the phone screen showing a calendar with one day circled, small city houses behind
say: A gift that can be taken back is not a gift. It is a leash.
You stay in the job. In the city. In the marriage that ended.
Because the payment is due on Tuesday.
The fear of death never went away.
(low) It just moved into the billing department.

shots.prompt: a dull office counter with a sign reading "BILLING DEPARTMENT", a bored robot clerk behind it with a stamp, a queue of people holding small white pills, fluorescent ceiling light

prompt: a person sitting on the edge of a bed at dawn, holding a phone, a window with the first light of day, a cup of coffee on the nightstand, quiet room, lots of white space
color: the dawn light in the window, pale orange
say: And yet.
A life that can be taken back is a life you finally count.
For a hundred thousand years we lived on credit without knowing the balance.
Every morning, the buzz. And with it a question no king ever had to answer:
(ask) Is today worth what it [costs](+2)?

prompt: a smartphone screen in close-up showing "PAYMENT FAILED" in big letters, behind it an enormous document titled "TERMS OF SERVICE" with thousands of pages fanning out, a tiny worried person peeking from behind the pages
say: (ask) So... what happens if you [miss](+2) a payment?
(pause) The terms of service have four thousand pages.
(pause 1.5, dramatic) The answer is on the last one.
